(a) 
        (1) Subsection (a) of section 101 of the Higher Education Facilities Act of 1963 is amended by striking out “during the fiscal year ending June 30, 1964, and each of the seven succeeding fiscal years.”. 
        (2) 
Subsection (b) of section 101 of such Act is amended by striking out so much of the first sentence thereof as follows “June 30, 1968, and” and inserting in lieu thereof “$936,000,000 for each of the succeeding fiscal years ending prior to July 1, 1971.”.
 
        (3) 
Subsection (b) of section 105 of such Act is amended (A) by striking out “two succeeding fiscal years” in the first sentence, thereof and inserting in lieu thereof “four succeeding fiscal years”, and (B) by striking out the last sentence of such subsection.
 
        (4) 
Section 103(b) (1) and section 104(b) (1) of such Act are each amended by striking out the last sentence.  
    (b) Section 201 of the Higher Education Facilities Act of 1963 is amended—

        (1) 
in the first sentence, by striking out “, during the fiscal year ending June 30, 1964, and each of the seven succeeding fiscal years,”; and
 
        (2) 
by striking out so much of the second sentence as follows “and the sum of $120,000,000” and inserting in lieu thereof “for each of the succeeding fiscal years ending prior to July 1, 1971.”.  
    (c) Subsection (c) of section 303 of the Higher Education Facilities Act of 1963 is amended—

        (1) 
in the first sentence thereof by striking out “, during the fiscal year ending June 30, 1964, and each of the seven succeeding fiscal years,”; and
 
        (2) 
in the second sentence thereof by striking out so much of such sentence as follows “$400,000,000” and inserting in lieu thereof “for each of the succeeding fiscal years ending prior to July 1, 1971.”.

fable.w: The section only amends the Higher Education Facilities Act of 1963 by striking and inserting text to extend fiscal-year authorizations and change appropriation amounts. The tempting reading is that amending a grant program for higher education facilities implies state or institutional involvement, but nothing here provides for consultation, hearings, rulemaking, advisory bodies, or a right to sue. No party outside the federal government is brought into any federal decision.

opus.w: This section only amends funding amounts and fiscal-year time limits in the Higher Education Facilities Act of 1963. It sets up no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking authority or right to sue for anyone outside the federal government. The Act is about grants to outside institutions, but grant applications are not participation, and this text does not even address how grants are applied for.
opus.b: 1. **Brief reasoning.** It might be tempting to say Yes because the Higher Education Facilities Act deals with grants to colleges and states. That reading fails for two reasons. First, the section only changes appropriation amounts and fiscal-year deadlines. Second, the definition excludes applications for benefits or grants from participation anyway. Nothing here calls for consultation, a hearing, a comment period, an advisory body, rulemaking or a right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section consists entirely of amendments to appropriation levels and fiscal years within the Higher Education Facilities Act. It does not establish any advisory committees, public comment periods, consultations with states or tribes, or rights to sue. It merely adjusts funding amounts and deadlines. Therefore, it does not involve participation by parties outside the federal government in a decision-making process.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because this section amends the Higher Education Facilities Act, which involves grants to universities (outside entities), it implies participation. However, the text itself only changes dollar amounts and timeframes for appropriations. It does not establish any new process for consultation, comment, or coordination with outside parties. The definition explicitly excludes "applications for benefits or grants" and requires an active mechanism for outside involvement in a decision. This section is purely fiscal/administrative.
